input: Hire a tutor for my teenager's algebra class

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the specific algebra level (Algebra 1, Algebra 2, pre-calculus, etc.) determines what expertise the tutor must have and narrows the candidate pool significantly.

Understanding the teenager's current struggles vs. goals (e.g., failing grades vs. aiming for an A) shapes whether they need remedial help, test prep, or enrichment, which affects the type of tutor to seek.
Whether sessions are in-person or online, and where, determines which platforms or local resources to use and what scheduling is feasible.
The budget per session or per month is a hard filter that eliminates or opens up entire categories of tutors (marketplace freelancers, tutoring centers, private professionals).
Session frequency and availability (e.g., weekday evenings, weekends) must align with the teenager's school and activity schedule, directly affecting which tutors are viable.

Preferences around tutor background (e.g., certified teacher, college student, professional tutor) or teaching style (patient and slow-paced vs. rigorous and fast) affect which candidate is the right fit.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like (a specific grade improvement, passing an upcoming exam, building long-term confidence) defines the timeline and how to evaluate whether the tutoring is working.

gold.taskTitle: Hire an algebra tutor for your teenager
gold.taskDescription: Find and hire a suitable tutor to help the user's teenager with their algebra class.

questions.title: Which algebra course specifically does your teenager need help with?
questions.description: Identify the exact course level — Algebra 1, Algebra 2, Pre-Algebra, or a combined/honors variant — so the tutor's required expertise is clear.

questions.title: What is the main reason tutoring is needed right now?
questions.description: Clarify whether the teenager is struggling with failing grades, preparing for a specific test, or looking to get ahead — this shapes the tutoring approach.

questions.title: Should sessions be in-person at home, or is online tutoring acceptable?
questions.description: Determine the preferred format and location for sessions, which determines whether to search local listings or online tutoring platforms.

questions.title: What is your budget per tutoring session?
questions.description: Establish a per-session or monthly spending limit to filter tutors by price range across different platforms and service types.

questions.title: How many sessions per week do you want, and on which days?
questions.description: Pin down the desired frequency and available time slots to match with tutors whose schedules align.

questions.title: Do you have a preference for the tutor's background or teaching style?
questions.description: Find out if the parent prefers a certified teacher, a college student, or a professional tutor, and whether a patient or more rigorous style is preferred.

questions.title: What specific outcome would make this tutoring a clear success?
questions.description: Define the measurable goal — such as a target grade, passing a semester exam, or building lasting confidence — to set a timeline and evaluation standard.
